chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, who said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj saying:

I saw Abu Abd al-Malik al-Qummi asking Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about inserting his hand into his garment during prayer in prostration. He said: 'If you wish, you do it; I do not fear for you regarding this.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) (Imam al-Sadiq)
key_terms.إِدْخَالِ يَدِهِ فِي الثَّوْبِ: Inserting the hand into the garment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on putting the hand inside the garment during prostration in prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Abu Abd al-Malik al-Qummi inquires of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the permissibility of inserting the hand into the garment during prostration. The Imam’s response, 'If you wish, you may do it; I do not fear for you from this,' signifies that while not obligatory, it is a valid and acceptable practice (ja'iz) that does not invalidate the prayer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on flexibility in non-essential acts of worship.
